newsitem.title: KENYA: Ugandan rebels dismiss Museveni's presence on front.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan rebels dismiss Museveni's presence on front.

text.p: Rebels in northern Uganda dismissed on Tuesday President Yoweri Museveni's decision to take command in the war against them, saying he would be lucky to survive.

Museveni has spent much of the past six weeks in the northern town of Gulu in an attempt to finish off the chronic rebellion by the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA), a Christian fundamentalist group with roots in the local Acholi people.
But LRA secretary general Dominic Wanyama, in a statement released in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, said Museveni's presence had failed to intimidate his movement.

"We are not cowards and therefore not threatened or scared of Museveni's militarist presence at the war front. We know for sure that...death is calling him here rather than the military victory which he stupidly expects. This is the kicking of a dying horse!" he said.
"Museveni will be (lucky) to survive up to the end of the war at the front line where he has placed himself," he added.

The war between the Ugandan army and Acholi rebels in various guises began soon after Museveni took power in 1986. The Ugandan government says Sudan is backing the LRA while Sudan accuses Uganda of backing its own rebels in southern Sudan.
Wanyama said Museveni had used the conflict to extract military support from Western countries and was now using this weaponry to carve out a Tutsi homeland in central Africa.
Museveni, a Hima from western Uganda, has ethnic links with the Tutsis who dominate the Rwandan army and the Banyamulenge rebels who have seized a swath of territory in eastern Zaire.
Wanyama's statement gave no up-to-date information on the military situation in the war in northern Uganda.
